title: hotfix: stabilize-slo-enforcer-backoff-regional-thrashing
author: Aisha Patel
description: Hotfix to address SLO enforcer thrashing observed under cross-regional failover during recent traffic spikes. Root cause: under certain rapid failover+backoff sequences the enforcer could apply duplicate backoff timers and race at coordinator level, causing transient over-shedding in healthy regions. This change stabilizes ordering and deduplicates backoff windows, adds additional guards for concurrent schedule updates, and restores previous steady-state behavior. Changes include: 1) introduce an ordering key for backoff events to ensure deterministic application on coordinator; 2) deduplicate scheduled backoff entries by (route, region, ordering_key); 3) add fast-path when enforcer observes identical backoff window across peers to avoid requeueing; 4) add provenance metadata to enforcer metrics and traces so we can correlate scheduling and operator-initiated overrides; 5) extend unit and integration tests to cover backoff ordering and dedup scenarios; 6) temporary release flag (slo.enforcer.backoff_dedupe) to allow canary rollout. Checklist: - reproduce locally with perf-canary (done) - add integration test covering regional failover ordering (done) - add metric+trace provenance (done) - staged rollout to prod: canary in us-west-2 -> staged to remaining regions (done) - post-merge monitoring playbook documented (done). Rollback plan: flip slo.enforcer.backoff_dedupe flag to false and revert coordinator ordering change if regression observed. Related: ENG-4129, ENG-4131, SUP-2918. This is a production hotfix; target merge into main and cherry-pick to release/2026-02-branch.
